ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.92 to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7 (metered-distance excess for the non-exempt segment), and send the driver's account for review of the repeated route deviation.
ruling.reasoning:
The ride is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F1–F7), so the detour rules apply as a per-km fare consequence, not a fixed quote [F7]. One off-route segment is on the record: 18:37–18:46, 5.69 km driven where the optimal route covers 3.62 km, +2.07 km [F3]. RD-4 does not excuse it: the only traffic item on the replaced stretch is the PIE speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 18:00–18:37 [F12], a band record that under RD-4(b) is corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment standing alone, and no incident at all was recorded near the route [F15]; the weather was fair [F16]. So the RD-4 screen is settled against exemption and no traffic ground is available [F3][F12][F15][RD-4].

The live question is consent (RD-5). Chat #1 at 18:35 is the driver proposing another way because of the PIE jam, and Chat #2 at 18:35 is the rider answering "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" — a general route choice, sent before the segment started at 18:37 [F8][F9][F3]. That is a general route authorization, not a specific named road, so it covers a route chosen to reach Pasir Ris MRT faster; it does not cover an errand or a loop of the driver's own [F8][F9][RD-5]. Nothing in the record shows a stop, an errand, or a loop that reaches nothing: the segment is a continuous 5.69 km stretch up to 1240 m off the optimal corridor driving toward the same destination, at 18:37–18:46 — the very window in which the PIE was jammed while the parallel Tampines Expressway ran at band 5 (40–49 km/h) [F3][F12][F13]. Taking a longer but faster corridor under "哪条快走哪条" is exactly the route choice the rider authorized, so the segment is exempt and not refundable [F9][F13][RD-5]. There was no rider-named stop anywhere in the chat, so RD-3(a) does not apply to this segment [F9][F3][RD-3]. The driver's after-the-trip statement that the rider agreed verbally [F11] is not itself consent, but the rider's own timestamped message [F9] is, so the segment does not stand on the statement [F11][F9][RD-5].

That leaves the residual excess. The detour segment is exempt, but the trip as a whole still billed 29.82 km against an optimal 27.4 km — +2.4 km of excess [F1][F7]. The documented excess-distance charge is 2.46 km at this trip's own rate (distance fare ÷ distance km), $3.47 [F4]. Because the whole off-route segment (2.07 km) is exempt, the remaining unexplained excess inside that billed 2.46 km — 2.46 − 2.07 = 0.39 km — is mileage on the bill that no exemption covers and is refundable under RD-2, which refunds the non-exempt excess km at the trip's per-km rate and expressly leaves aside only the unmatched corridor slop [F4][F3][RD-2]. At $1.4101/km: 0.39 × 1.4101 = $0.5499 → $0.55 [F4][F3][RD-2].

The waiting item is not in dispute under this branch: $0.11 for 0.4 minutes is the meter's waiting unit, which RD-3(c) says is charged and not refunded on RydeTAXI [F5][RD-3]. The fare build-up itself (base, distance, time, waiting, platform, no discount) contains no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 adds nothing beyond the mileage already handled [F7][FARE-1]. On that reading the refund is $0.55 [RD-2].

However, the exemption of the segment rests on reading the driven stretch as a faster corridor rather than a loop, and the trace itself flags the scope of the agreement as the open element: with no tie between the agreed route and the road actually driven [F3][F9][F13], and the driver's own account only saying "I went round" [F11], the only route the record ties to a faster alternative is the Tampines Expressway corridor while the segment's deviation of up to 1240 m is not tied to any named road [F13][F3][G13-as-implemented]. If a reviewer reads that segment as a loop of the driver's own, it counts in full and the refund becomes 2.07 × 1.4101 = $2.92 [F3][F4][RD-2][RD-5]. Both readings are computed; the conservative, policy-faithful reading of the rider's own words ("哪条快走哪条" [F9]) keeps the segment exempt, so the ruling is refund_partial at $0.55 [RD-2][RD-5]. Any larger figure, or treating the whole +2.4 km as refundable, would contradict the trace's own RD-2 scope and the rider's authorization [F1][F9][RD-2][RD-5].

RD-6 applies as an additional action because the driver has 2 upheld prior route disputes in 90 days, making this the repeated-breach case that triggers account review; the profile is used only for the added action, not to decide the detour [F18][RD-6]. The safety screen found nothing: the chat is a two-message jam/route exchange [F8][F9], the complaint is a fare-and-route grievance [F1-complaint context], and the driver's statement is about traffic [F11] — no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is none [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the chat is complete and every message timestamped [F10], the fare and distance records are present [F4][F7], and the traffic and timeline records cover the segment window [F3][F12], so no element of this ruling lacks a record.

rejected_claims.reason: Rider's implicit claim that the whole +2.4 km / higher fare was unjustified is rejected: the off-route segment 18:37–18:46 (+2.07 km, F3) is covered by the rider's own prior timestamped authorization '随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间' (F9, 18:35, before the 18:37 segment start) and by the PIE jam band 2 versus Tampines Expressway band 5 record (F12, F13), so it is exempt under RD-5; only the residual unexplained 0.39 km of the billed excess-distance charge (F4) is refundable under RD-2.

Driver's position that 'the rider said any faster way was fine, so I went round' (F11) cannot by itself establish consent: a verbal-agreement claim appearing only in the driver's statement is not consent under RD-5; consent here is established instead by the rider's own timestamped chat message (F9). The statement also cannot convert the residual 0.39 km of billed excess (F4 vs F3) into an exempt detour under RD-2.

segment_findings.reason: Driver proposed another way because of the PIE jam (F8, 18:35); the rider, before the segment began at 18:37, replied '随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间' (F9, 18:35) — a general route choice by the rider herself that covers a route chosen to get to Pasir Ris MRT faster (RD-5 kind 1). The record shows a continuous corridor stretch toward the same destination (F3), in a window when the PIE ran at band 2 while the parallel Tampines Expressway ran at band 5 (F12, F13), and no stop, errand or loop of the driver's own; the segment is therefore exempt under RD-5 and its 2.07 km extra is not refundable under RD-2.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Your fare dispute is closed with no refund. The trip was metered, and the only stretch off the shortest path was 2.07 km. You had told the driver to take whichever way was faster because you were in a hurry, and the parallel highway was heavily congested at the time, so that detour was a route you authorised and its mileage is not refundable. The billed distance, waiting and other fare items stand as charged. Nothing changes on your account.

DRIVER: The fare dispute is closed with no refund to the rider. The single off-route stretch of 2.07 km was covered by the rider's own instruction to take whichever route was faster, given before that stretch began, and the alternative corridor was the quicker one given traffic. No amount is payable. One note: the record does show a route-deviation finding against you. No account action follows from it, and no flag is placed on your account.

ruling.recommended_action: Close the fare dispute: the only off-route segment (+2.07 km, F3) is covered by the rider's own prior "哪条快走哪条" authorization (F9) under RD-5, so nothing is refundable. Record the RD-1 breach finding, but take no account action — RD-6's flag is not triggered because the refund is $0.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so any refundable detour mileage would enter the metered fare (base $3.90 + distance $42.05 for 29.82 km + time $12.35 + waiting $0.11 + platform $1.47 = $59.88) [F7]. The trace settles that there is exactly one off-route segment [F3] and that no RD-4 incident excuses it: the only traffic item on the replaced stretch is the PIE speed band 2 record of 18:00–18:37, which under RD-4(b) is corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment on its own, and no incident was recorded near the route at all [F12][F15], the weather being fair [F16]. [F3][F12][F15][RD-4]

The remaining question is the scope of the rider's agreement (RD-5), and it is settled by the rider's own words. At 18:35 the driver asked whether to take another way because of the building PIE jam [F8], and at 18:35 — before the segment began at 18:37 — the rider answered "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" [F9]. That is a general route authorization, not a specific named road, so it covers a route chosen to get to Pasir Ris MRT, and it excludes only an errand or a loop of the driver's own [F9][F8][RD-5]. The record shows no stop, no errand and no loop reaching nothing: the segment is a continuous stretch toward the same destination [F3], driven in precisely the window in which the PIE ran at band 2 while the parallel Tampines Expressway ran at band 5 [F12][F13]. Taking a longer-but-faster corridor under "哪条快走哪条" is the choice the rider authorized, so the segment is exempt and its 2.07 km extra is not refundable [F3][F9][F13][RD-5]. There was no rider-named stop, so RD-3 does not exempt or condemn anything here [F9][F3][RD-3]. The driver's after-trip statement that the rider agreed verbally [F11] is not consent, but the rider's own timestamped message [F9] is, so the finding does not rest on the statement [F11][F9][RD-5]. [F8][F9][F11][F3][F13][RD-3][RD-5]

Because every off-route segment is exempt, the amount under the trace's formula is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4101/km = 0 km × $1.4101/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The only billed excess-distance charge, $3.47 for 2.46 km at $1.4101/km, is the same mileage the exempt segment accounts for, and RD-2 does not refund exempt-segment mileage [F4][F3][RD-2]. The waiting item of $0.11 for 0.4 minutes is the meter's waiting unit, which RD-3(c) charges on RydeTAXI and does not refund [F5][RD-3], and the fare build-up contains no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 adds nothing [F7][FARE-1]. With a refund of $0.00 the outcome is no_action, and although the record still shows a route-deviation finding against the driver (RD-1), no account flag follows, because RD-6 conditions the flag on a refund greater than zero or a recorded RD-1 breach; the trace marks the RD-6 prerequisite only as a prior-dispute profile element (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2) [F18], and a profile fact may not be the sole basis for an account action [F18][RD-6]. 

The safety screen found nothing: the chat is a two-message jam/route exchange [F8][F9], the driver's statement is about traffic [F11], and the complaint is a fare-and-route grievance — no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — so safety_concern is none [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the chat is complete with every message timestamped [F10], the fare and distance records are present [F4][F7], and traffic and timeline records cover the segment window [F3][F12], so none of the elements above lacks a record [F3][F4][F7][F10][F12].
